channel.title: Crypto Record
channel.description: Crypto Record reports news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation and network upgrades across the crypto market.

item.title: Swift readies blockchain ledger for 17-bank payment pilot
item.description: Swift says 17 banks are preparing live cross-border payment pilots on its blockchain ledger, using tokenized deposits to move funds around the clock.

item.title: OCC leaves stablecoin rewards to case-by-case review
item.description: The OCC’s GENIUS Act rule bars issuers from paying stablecoin interest but leaves exchange rewards to case-by-case review, shaping how crypto firms compete.

item.title: How to Trade Through Fermi Swap and Verify the Fill
item.description: Fermi swap trades run through a wallet-signed Ethereum transaction; check the receipt, token transfers and swap event to confirm what actually filled.

item.title: How Much Gas Should You Keep on the Destination Chain?
item.description: Keep enough of the destination chain’s native token for the first action after a bridge; the right reserve depends on the route and transaction.

item.title: SyncSwap: How a first swap and liquidity deposit work
item.description: SyncSwap swaps tokens through on-chain pools and lets users deposit assets to earn a share of fees, with price and liquidity risks to weigh first.

item.title: Chainflip swaps: how deposits become native-asset payouts
item.description: Chainflip records deposits on its State Chain, prices swaps against virtual liquidity, then validators sign native-asset payouts; fees combine pool, protocol and chain costs.

item.title: Mastercard opens AI agent payment APIs after six pilots
item.description: Mastercard opened Agent Pay for Machines to developers after pilots, using signed x402 payment vouchers to let AI agents buy services within approved budgets.

item.title: Five checks to make before using a relay bridge
item.description: A relay bridge moves assets through contracts on two chains. Check the network, addresses, code, permissions and wallet request before approving a transfer.

item.title: Why Crypto Bridges Take Days, and When Speed Is Worth It
item.description: A bridge’s quoted time depends on how it verifies and settles transfers. Learn what can take days, what faster routes change, and how to choose.

item.title: JPMorgan brings deposit token JPM Coin to Ethereum
item.description: JPMorgan has extended JPM Coin to Ethereum, giving institutional clients another public network for moving dollar deposits between EVM-compatible wallets.

item.title: Revolut wins Gibraltar crypto licence for global services
item.description: Revolut’s Gibraltar permission covers crypto orders, custody and staking, giving its new subsidiary a regulatory base for international services whose markets remain unannounced.

item.title: Circle says USDC reinvestment leaves 7 cents per revenue dollar
item.description: Circle says it kept seven cents of each USDC revenue dollar in H1 2026, as Coinbase backs a rival model that sends reserve income to partners after a fee.

item.title: Ledger reviews wallet sales after $93 million crypto drain
item.description: Ledger is reviewing reseller sales and device tamper defenses after an implant-linked drain; analysts traced about $93 million, which Ledger has not confirmed.

item.title: Ledger reviews sales controls after wallet implant theft
item.description: Ledger is reviewing how its wallets reach buyers after an implant in reseller units captured recovery phrases and sent them over LTE to attackers.

item.title: Coinbase and Marqeta team up on stablecoin-backed cards
item.description: Coinbase will custody stablecoins and convert them to fiat for Marqeta card programs, with Base handling settlement and businesses able to fund programs 24/7.

item.title: Funding a Protocol on Another Chain Starts With the Asset
item.description: Funding a protocol on another chain means moving the right asset to its network, keeping gas for fees, then depositing through the protocol’s own contract.

item.title: Why volatile swaps can fill worse
item.description: A swap can fill below its quote when pool prices move before execution; MEV searchers can add pressure, while minimum-output limits cap what you accept.

item.title: Why Swap Fees Drift Between Quote and Execution
item.description: Swap fee drift is the gap between a swap’s estimated and final costs, caused by changing pool prices, route fees, network gas and execution conditions.

item.title: Why a Cross-Chain Swap Can Wait on Destination Gas
item.description: A cross-chain swap can stay pending after its input arrives because validators still need to observe, execute and fund the destination-chain payout from the quoted output.

item.title: Why a Calldata Change Can Break a Signed Swap
item.description: A swap signature covers specific transaction bytes or typed fields; changing calldata can break that authorization or change execution when the signed fields leave it open.
